purpose: Cover-production contract for Rex Fleet Academy: Between the Beacons. Issue 1 establishes a repeatable Academy/topic cover identity built around transfer of knowledge through visually compelling science and engineering demonstrations, then becomes the approved masthead/trade-dress pixel reference for any later cover. Later issue recipes control their own subject and demonstration.

foundingCover.activationRule: Do not treat this path as visual authority until the Issue 1 cover is explicitly approved and the exact approved pixels are persisted at this path.
foundingCover.approvalWriteback: After approval/persistence, change foundingCover.state to approved-trade-dress-reference and status to active, then record the asset SHA if the production workflow provides one.

controls: recurring cover margins and trade-dress geometry
overall Between the Beacons cover-brand recognition

pixelReadGate.rule: Before generating any later Between the Beacons cover added after Issue 1, retrieve and inspect the actual approved Issue 1 cover pixels in active multimodal context. A repository path, description, hash, thumbnail metadata, remembered image, or statement that the cover was previously viewed does not satisfy this gate.
pixelReadGate.blockedBehavior: If a later cover is added and the Issue 1 approved cover pixels do not yet exist or cannot be visually inspected, stop before later-cover generation and complete the Issue 1 cover bootstrap first.

recipeAuthority.rule: The assembled current cover recipe controls the issue-specific selling image, cast, setting, composition, spoiler ceiling, and exact required trade-dress text. The approved Issue 1 cover controls only recurring cover-brand appearance at the scope above.
recipeAuthority.conflictResolution: If copying Issue 1 composition would conflict with a later issue recipe, follow the current issue recipe and preserve only the scoped trade-dress continuity.

coverRules: The primary selling idea is transfer of knowledge: make a difficult feature of the world visible through an Academy lecture demonstration, engineering experiment, simulation, field practicum, or comparable act of learning.
Prefer instructor/student interaction with active manipulation, observation, error, measurement, or realization over infrastructure-only spectacle.
One dominant scientific, engineering, cultural, historical, or institutional question per cover.
No generic cast lineup or professor-at-podium composition.
No textbook page, detached infographic, or wall of explanatory HUD text.
Scientific visualizations must preserve established fictional physics rather than defaulting to magical portals or decorative energy effects.
Only exact required cover lettering and explicitly permitted canonical notation may be rendered.
The cover must remain legible and compelling at thumbnail size.
Do not reveal the issue's decisive solution, late reversal, or final image.
Use wider-world infrastructure as context or consequence when useful, but the Academy act of understanding is the visual/emotional center.
